title: Varying the Faithfulness Metric in Circuit Evaluation: Does Choice of Ablation Type Change Which Circuit Is Found Best?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if the best circuit under one metric fails under another, published interpretability results may be metric artifacts. This directly undermines trust in circuits claimed to explain safety-relevant behavior. Every link from 'metric comparison' to 'trust in published results' is explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running both ACDC and attribution patching with three ablation types on the IOI task. Understanding the differences between zero, mean, and resample ablation and correctly implementing the cross-metric evaluation requires familiarity with circuit-finding methodology. Advanced for beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: one task (IOI), two methods x three ablation types, a 3x2 confusion matrix of cross-metric faithfulness. Clear experimental design with a single well-defined output artifact. ~10 hours compute fits within 30-hour budget.

novelty.reasoning: Chughtai et al., 'Transformer Circuit Faithfulness Metrics Are Not Robust' (arXiv:2407.08734, COLM 2024) directly addresses this question. They show that existing faithfulness metrics are highly sensitive to ablation methodology (zero, mean, resample), with resample ablations producing systematically lower faithfulness than mean ablations (p=1e-5). The proposed 3x2 confusion matrix of cross-metric faithfulness on IOI is a subset of what this published paper already demonstrates. Additionally, Li & Janson, 'Optimal ablation for interpretability' (arXiv:2409.09951) further extends this line of work.
